# characters had other readings in the classics (說 shuō, also yuè "pleased").

column4: Classical Chinese is written in characters, each standing for a word or a part of one; the same written language was read across China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam for two thousand years.

column2: Chinese characters in their traditional forms, the standard shapes since the Han dynasty; the classics were written in columns, top to bottom and right to left, with no punctuation.

Tap the characters, or find one by its pinyin (xue, dao, ren …) in the search box: each comes with its reading and meaning. “Top to bottom” sets the picture in columns from right to left, as books were printed until the 20th century.

column4: the Way; a road; to speak
